newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms to export $124 mln in China oil barter.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms to export $124 mln in China oil barter.

text.p: Yugoslav companies have concluded around $124.6 million worth of export deals under a barter arrangement with China in exchange for crude oil, the Serbian Chamber of Commerce said on Tuesday.

Serbia's oil company Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS) and Chinese state oil concern Sinochem signed a barter deal in March 1996 for imports of two million tonnes of crude from China in exchange for products of the Yugoslav metallurgy, machine building, chemical and other industries.

The one-year deal was to have been carried out by April 1997 but was extended into a five-year contract during a session of the inter-government Chinese-Yugoslav commission in Belgrade last month, the chamber said in a report presented at a meeting of its board of directors.
According to the chamber's report, the Yugoslav side has presented Sinochem with offers from 167 enterprises worth a total of $3.3 billion.
So far seven contracts worth $124.6 million dollars have been signed.
The 14 Oktobar plant of Krusevac concluded a five-year deal for the delivery of construction machinery and caterpillar tractors worth $38.4 million dollars to China.
Industrija motora i traktora (IMT) of Belgrade will deliver 1,000 tractors worth $22 million to a Chinese partner over a period of two years.
Zmaj Zemun has signed a contract for 500 maize harvesters and 200 combines worth $9.2 million, while machine tools manufacturer Lola corporation will export $1.6 million.
The Sartid steel works of Smederevo has concluded $30 million worth of exports and Viskoza of Loznica $37.2 million worth of viscose fibres exports.
Cer of Cacak will deliver processing equipment for dried vegetables worth $850,000, the report said.
It gave no details about the value or quantities of Chinese crude delivered to date on the basis of the barter arrangement. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
